The element inventory and exact Jmol/VESTA values come from `../e04_t10/published-elements.tsv`, whose independent upstream capture is documented there. The generator writes one P1 site per element on a six-Angstrom Cartesian grid. A separate small structure supplies the linked diffraction calculation, so opening the colour witness does not calculate diffraction from the complete element inventory.

The colour assertions use the existing independent W3C luminance and Ottosson Oklab reference. Hue stays fixed; chroma is the maximum that fits sRGB at the resulting Oklab lightness. Both retain the independent half-LSB RGB quantisation bounds. The complete table is observed through one real delegate while the two real legends are captured before those input edits. P1 coordinates identify sphere instances independently of the engine's site ordering.

Qt Quick 3D stores its instance colours through a monotone cubic conversion rather than the exact WCAG transfer. The independent decoder uses the coefficients published in [Qt 6.11.2 qssgutils.cpp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt/qtquick3d/v6.11.2/src/utils/qssgutils.cpp), `QSSGUtils::color::sRGBToLinear`; [qquick3dinstancing.cpp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt/qtquick3d/v6.11.2/src/quick3d/qquick3dinstancing.cpp) documents the actual table conversion and readback. It identifies the original byte on that lattice, including the low-channel values where applying WCAG's inverse would be wrong. The strict W3C computation remains separate for every 2D contrast assertion.

The real atom-sites and parameter-name delegates also execute every published element on both alternating rows and each row's hovered state, on both themes. Gap pixels between cells identify the rendered underlay independently of the page colour; the frozen upstream style fixture checks those pixels. Parameter rows retain actual atom coordinate items in a supplied two-row placement model. A default table colour may conservatively cover all three underlays; a published colour that already passes on all of them retains its bytes. The carbon witness separates page-white contrast from alternating and hovered-row contrast. Separate bounded actor invocations retain the original watchdog.
